full_judgment: 23. It is further submitted by Mr. Toufique Newaz that the respondent-company is commercially insolvent and if a company is commercially insolvent, it is liable to be wound up. He has referred to the cases of the Punjab Flying Club Limited, AIR 1933 (Lahore), 301 and M/s. Vanaspati Industries Ltd. v- Firm Prabhu Dayal Hari Ram, AIR 1950 (East Punjub), 142. In the aforesaid two decisions it is held by their Lordships that if a company is insolvent or if a company is unable to run its business or if the company stops its business, then it will be deemed that it is commercially insolvent and for that reason the company is liable to be wound up. Mr. Toufique Newaz has urged the point, but he has not been able to produce any materials before this Court to show that the company is commercially insolvent, rather from the records it appears that the respondent company has been running its business. Not only that the respondent-company has been repaying its debts substantially to the creditors from time to time. On this point of Mr. Toufique Newaz I do not find any substance. Considering the above I am led to hold that the petitioners have not been able to prove that the company is unable to pay its debts.
